4423.stem: A student believes that the time it takes for an ice cube to melt ($M$ minutes) varies inversely with the room temperature ($T^\circ\text{C}$). The student observes that at a room temperature of $15^\circ\text{C}$ it takes 12 minutes for an ice cube to melt.

figures.cap: blank grid: time M (minutes) against temperature T
solution sketch: graph of M = 180/T

parts.latex: Find the equation relating $M$ and $T$.

solutions.latex:
Inverse variation means $M = \dfrac{k}{T}$.

When $T = 15$, $M = 12$.
$$\begin{aligned} 12 &= \dfrac{k}{15} \\ k &= 15 \times 12 \\ &= 180 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ M = \dfrac{180}{T}$$
criteria: Writes down an equation representing inverse variation, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Trish is planning a function. The cost per person to attend the function varies inversely with the number of people attending.

The cost per person is \$70 when 50 people attend.

What is the cost per person if 125 people attend the function?

solutions.latex:
The cost varies inversely with the number of people, so
$$C = \dfrac{k}{n}$$
Substituting $C = 70$, $n = 50$:
$$\begin{aligned} 70 &= \dfrac{k}{50} \\ k &= 70 \times 50 = 3500 \end{aligned}$$
So $C = \dfrac{3500}{n}$. When $n = 125$:
$$\begin{aligned} C &= \dfrac{3500}{125} \\ &= \$28 \text{ per person} \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
The time taken to clean a warehouse varies inversely with the number of cleaners employed.

It takes 8 cleaners 60 hours to clean a warehouse.

Working at the same rate, how many hours would it take 10 cleaners to clean the same warehouse?

solutions.latex:
Time varies inversely with the number of cleaners $n$, so $T=\dfrac{k}{n}$.

When $n=8$ and $T=60$:
$$k=8\times 60=480$$
When $n=10$:
$$T=\dfrac{480}{10}=48 \text{ hours}$$
So option B is correct.

parts.latex:
The time taken to paint a school varies inversely with the number of painters completing the task.

It takes 6 painters a total of 20 days to paint a school.

How many days would it take 15 painters to paint the same school?

solutions.latex:
Time varies inversely with the number of painters, so $t = \dfrac{k}{n}$, that is, $k = nt$ is constant.

From 6 painters taking 20 days:
$$k = 6 \times 20 = 120$$
For 15 painters:
$$t = \dfrac{120}{15} = 8 \text{ days}$$
This is option B.

parts.latex:
The time taken ($t$) to clean a house varies inversely with the number of people ($p$) cleaning the house.

Which graph illustrates this relationship?

solutions.latex:
Inverse variation means $t = \dfrac{k}{p}$ for a constant $k>0$.

As $p$ increases, $t$ decreases but never reaches 0 (it gets close to the $p$-axis). As $p$ gets close to 0, $t$ becomes very large (it gets close to the $t$-axis).

This is a hyperbola, decreasing and curving towards both axes. A straight line (A, C) is not inverse variation, and D is increasing.

$$\therefore\ \text{Graph B}$$

parts.latex:
The thickness of the skin of a spherical balloon varies inversely with the surface area of the balloon.

What would be the effect on the thickness of the skin if the radius of the balloon is doubled?

solutions.latex:
Let the thickness be $t$ and the surface area $A = 4\pi r^2$. Inverse variation gives
$$t = \dfrac{k}{A} = \dfrac{k}{4\pi r^2}$$
If $r$ becomes $2r$, the surface area becomes
$$4\pi (2r)^2 = 4\times 4\pi r^2$$
so the area is multiplied by 4, and the thickness is divided by 4.

Hence the correct option is C.

meta.self_check: Area scales with r squared, thickness inversely.

6071.stem: The volume of a gas in a balloon is inversely proportional to the pressure applied to compress it. Helium has a volume of $20\ \text{m}^3$ at a pressure of $9$ kPa.

parts.latex: Find the constant of variation.
What is the volume of helium at a pressure of $45$ kPa?
What pressure is necessary to compress the gas to $8\ \text{m}^3$?

solutions.latex:
For inverse proportion, $V = \dfrac{k}{P}$.

Substitute $V = 20$, $P = 9$.

$$\begin{aligned} 20 &= \dfrac{k}{9} \\ k &= 20 \times 9 \\ &= 180 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} V &= \dfrac{180}{P} \\ &= \dfrac{180}{45} \\ &= 4 \text{ m}^3 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} 8 &= \dfrac{180}{P} \\ P &= \dfrac{180}{8} \\ &= 22.5 \text{ kPa} \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex: The time taken to construct a garage is inversely proportional to the number of people working on the task. A group of 7 people can complete the task in 50 days. How many people will it take to construct the garage in 35 days?

solutions.latex:
For inverse proportion, $t = \dfrac{k}{p}$.

Substitute $p = 7$, $t = 50$.
$$\begin{aligned} 50 &= \dfrac{k}{7} \\ k &= 350 \end{aligned}$$
So $t = \dfrac{350}{p}$. Substitute $t = 35$.
$$\begin{aligned} 35 &= \dfrac{350}{p} \\ p &= \dfrac{350}{35} \\ &= 10 \end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ 10 people.

6391.stem:
An electrical circuit has a constant voltage applied and has a resistance which can be changed.

The amount of current in amps ($C$) which will flow in the circuit is inversely proportional to the resistance in Ohms ($R$) of the circuit.

The graph below shows the curve which demonstrates the relationship between $R$ and $C$ for this circuit.

\exfigure{308_q31_1}

figures.cap: inverse variation graph of current against resistance

parts.latex:
The equation which describes the curve is of the form $C = \dfrac{K}{R}$.

Use the point $(6, 40)$ on the graph to find the value of $K$.
What is the current in the circuit when it has the resistance set to $30\ \Omega$?
When the current is measured as 20 A, what is the resistance value?

solutions.latex:
The curve has equation $C = \dfrac{K}{R}$, and passes through $(6, 40)$.

Substitute $R = 6$, $C = 40$.
$$\begin{aligned} 40 &= \dfrac{K}{6} \\ K &= 40\times 6 \\ &= 240 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ K = 240$$

meta.self_check: Checked against graph: (10,24), (20,12), (30,8) all satisfy CR=240.

solutions.latex:
Using $C = \dfrac{240}{R}$ with $R = 30$:
$$\begin{aligned} C &= \dfrac{240}{30} \\ &= 8 \text{ A} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the current is } 8 \text{ A}$$

meta.self_check: Graph at R=30 reads about 8 A.

solutions.latex:
Using $C = \dfrac{240}{R}$ with $C = 20$:
$$\begin{aligned} 20 &= \dfrac{240}{R} \\ R &= \dfrac{240}{20} \\ &= 12\ \Omega \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the resistance is } 12\ \Omega$$

parts.latex: The maximum speed ($v$), in km/h, of a truck is inversely proportional to the weight ($w$ kg) it carries. A truck carrying a weight of 1600 kg can travel at 80 km/h. What is the maximum speed of the truck if the weight is 1250 kg

solutions.latex:
The speed is inversely proportional to the weight.
$$v=\dfrac{k}{w}$$
Substitute $v=80$ and $w=1600$.
$$\begin{aligned} 80 &= \dfrac{k}{1600} \\ k &= 80\times 1600 \\ &= 128\,000 \end{aligned}$$
So $v=\dfrac{128\,000}{w}$.

When $w=1250$:
$$\begin{aligned} v &= \dfrac{128\,000}{1250} \\ &= 102.4 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the speed is } 102.4 \text{ km/h}$$

6467.stem:
The operating loss, $L$ millions of dollars, of mining black opals in Lightning Ridge, varies inversely with the amount of opals mined, $M$ kilograms, according to the equation

$$L=\dfrac{k}{M}$$

The Lightning Ridge Mining Company lost 36 million dollars mining 3 kilograms of black opals.

parts.latex: Find the value of $k$.
What is the operating loss when 9.5 kilograms of black opals are mined, correct to three significant figures?

solutions.latex:
Substitute $L=36$ and $M=3$ into $L=\dfrac{k}{M}$.
$$\begin{aligned}36&=\dfrac{k}{3}\\ \therefore k&=108\end{aligned}$$

Substitute $k=108$ and $M=9.5$.
$$\begin{aligned}L&=\dfrac{108}{9.5}\\&=11.4\text{ million dollars}\quad\text{(correct to 3 significant figures)}\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ L\approx \$11.4 \text{ million}$$
criteria: Uses their value of $k$ from part (a), or equivalent merit

6510.stem:
The time taken for a colony of ants to break up a sandwich and carry it away to the nest is inversely proportional to the number of ants performing the task.

If there are 20 ants, then it takes 42 minutes for the sandwich to be taken to the nest.

parts.latex: Calculate how long it takes for 32 ants to carry the sandwich to the nest.

Another group of ants takes 1 hour and 10 minutes to carry the sandwich to the nest.

How many ants are in this group?

solutions.latex:
Time is inversely proportional to the number of ants, so with $t$ the time and $n$ the number of ants,
$$t = \dfrac{k}{n}$$
Substituting $t = 42$, $n = 20$:
$$\begin{aligned} 42 &= \dfrac{k}{20} \\ k &= 840 \end{aligned}$$
So $t = \dfrac{840}{n}$. When $n = 32$:
$$\begin{aligned} t &= \dfrac{840}{32} \\ &= 26.25 \text{ minutes} \\ &= 26 \text{ minutes } 15 \text{ seconds} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correctly calculates the constant of proportionality, or equivalent merit
Attempts to calculate the inverse proportionality, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
1 hour 10 minutes is $t = 70$ minutes.
$$\begin{aligned} 70 &= \dfrac{840}{n} \\ n &= \dfrac{840}{70} \\ &= 12 \text{ ants} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Converts time to minutes and substitutes, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
A preschool centre pays \$210 to hire a bus for an excursion. Let $C$ be the cost per person and $N$ be the number of people going on the excursion.

Write an equation connecting $C$ and $N$, if the cost per person is \$2.10. Hence, determine the number of people who travelled on the bus if the centre paid \$315.

solutions.latex:
The total cost is the hire fee plus $\$2.10$ per person, so $C = 210 + 2.10N$ (the question calls $C$ the cost per person, but $C$ here is the total the centre pays).

When the centre paid $\$315$:

$$\begin{aligned} 315 &= 210 + 2.10N \\ \dfrac{315 - 210}{2.10} &= N \\ N &= 50 \end{aligned}$$

$$\therefore\ 50 \text{ people travelled on the bus.}$$
criteria: Writes the equation, or equivalent merit

6622.stem:
The frequency ($F$) (number of vibrations per second) measured in Hertz (Hz), of a string on a harp, varies inversely with the square root of the length of the string ($L$) measured in cm.

A string of length 25 cm on a harp has frequency of 10 Hz.

parts.latex: Show that the situation can be modelled by the equation: $F=\dfrac{50}{\sqrt{L}}$
What length of string would produce a frequency of 12.5 Hz on the harp?

solutions.latex:
Substitute $L=25$ into the given model.
$$\begin{aligned} F &= \dfrac{50}{\sqrt{L}} \\ &= \dfrac{50}{\sqrt{25}} \\ &= \dfrac{50}{5} \\ &= 10 \text{ Hz} \end{aligned}$$
This agrees with the given frequency, so the model is shown.

Substitute $F=12.5$ into $F=\dfrac{50}{\sqrt{L}}$.
$$\begin{aligned} 12.5 &= \dfrac{50}{\sqrt{L}} \\ \sqrt{L} &= \dfrac{50}{12.5} \\ &= 4 \\ L &= 16 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the length is } 16 \text{ cm}$$
criteria: Substitutes $F=12.5$ and makes progress towards finding $L$, or equivalent merit

When people walk in snow, the depth ($D$ cm) of each footprint depends on both the area ($A$ cm$^2$) of the shoe sole and the weight of the person. The graph shows the relationship between the area of the shoe sole and the depth of the footprint in snow, for a group of people of the same weight.

parts.latex: The graph is a hyperbola because $D$ is inversely proportional to $A$. The point $P$ lies on the hyperbola. Find the equation relating $D$ and $A$.
A man from this group walks in snow and the depth of his footprint is 5 cm. Use your equation from part (i) to calculate the area of his shoe sole.

solutions.latex:
Since $D$ is inversely proportional to $A$, the equation has the form
$$D = \dfrac{k}{A}$$
From the graph, $P$ is the point $(300, 15)$, so substitute $A = 300$, $D = 15$.
$$\begin{aligned} 15 &= \dfrac{k}{300} \\ k &= 15\times 300 = 4500 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ D = \dfrac{4500}{A}$$
criteria: Reads the coordinates of $P$ and substitutes into $D = \dfrac{k}{A}$, or equivalent merit

$$\begin{aligned} 5 &= \dfrac{4500}{A} \\ A &= \dfrac{4500}{5} \\ &= 900 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the area of his shoe sole is } 900 \text{ cm}^2$$

parts.latex: If pressure ($P$) varies inversely with volume ($V$), write a formula to correctly express in terms of $P$ and $V$.

solutions.latex:
Inverse variation means $P$ is proportional to $\dfrac{1}{V}$, with constant $k$.
$$\therefore\ P=\dfrac{k}{V}$$
criteria: Shows inverse proportion with a constant, or equivalent merit
